findings.title: Prisma.sql object comparison fails for service-built nested SQL
findings.body: The service builds this team condition with `conditions.reduce((acc, condition) => Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})`)`, so the returned `Prisma.Sql` is composed of multiple nested `Prisma.Sql` fragments. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` compares the internal `strings` and `values` arrays, not the rendered SQL text, so the actual and expected structures will differ even though the SQL is semantically equivalent. The same issue affects the org-scope expectation near line 332 and the combined-filter expectation near line 429. The test should compare rendered SQL or explicitly flattened/normalized `strings`/`values`, and should be run to confirm.

findings.title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
findings.body: The previous class exposed `findMany(findManyArgs)` for querying `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`; this PR replaces it with `getBaseConditions()` returning raw `Prisma.Sql`. Only the service and its tests are changed in this diff, so any production code still calling `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or run when this is merged. If the service is used outside the test file, keep `findMany` as a thin wrapper or migrate all callers in the same PR.

findings.title: Caching tests removed for raw SQL conditions
findings.body: The old `describe("Caching")` tests verified that repeated calls to `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached values and do not rebuild. Those tests are deleted, but the caching logic remains in `insightsBooking.ts` (lines 83-94). Losing this coverage makes it easy to break caching with `Prisma.Sql` fragments without a failing test.
